activity_context.topic_title: Differentiating Curves Given in Polar Form

feedback.problem: Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the polar curve $r=12$ at $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use the formula for differentiating parametric curves:

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )}
$$

First, we recall that to convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

Using the fact that $r=12,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x=12\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=12\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating the necessary derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(\theta ) & =-12\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,{y}^{′}(\theta )=12\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{12\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{-12\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we arrive at

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =2\pi /3} & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}) \\  & =-(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
